body:
## Summary

Resolves 5 high-severity Dependabot security alerts by bumping parent dependencies rather than using blanket overrides where possible.

## Packages Updated

| Package | Old Constraint | New Constraint | Strategy | CVEs Resolved |
|---------|---------------|----------------|----------|---------------|
| `@langchain/core` | `^1.0.2` | `^1.1.28` | Direct bump | [CVE-2025-68665](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v34v-rq6j-cj6p) — serialization injection |
| `tailwindcss` | `^4.0.13` | `^4.2.1` | Parent bump | [CVE-2026-23745](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8qq5-rm4j-mr97), [CVE-2026-23950](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r6q2-hw4h-h46w), [CVE-2026-24842](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-34x7-hfp2-rc4v), [CVE-2026-26960](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-83g3-92jg-28cx) — removes `tar` dep from `@tailwindcss/oxide` entirely |
| `@tailwindcss/postcss` | `^4.0.13` | `^4.2.1` | Parent bump | Same tar CVEs |
| `eslint` | `^9.19.0` | `^9.39.3` | Parent bump | [CVE-2026-26996](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26) — pulls `@eslint/eslintrc@3.3.4` with `minimatch ^3.1.3` |
| `typescript-eslint` | `^8.22.0` | `^8.56.1` | Parent bump | CVE-2026-26996 — pulls `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree@8.56.1` with `minimatch@10` |
| `@playwright/test` | *(new devDep)* | `^1.58.2` | Explicit pin | [CVE-2025-59288](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp) — forces safe `playwright` version (was auto-resolved to `1.52.0` via Next.js optional peer dep) |

## Strategy C — pnpm.overrides (residual cases)

Some `minimatch@3.1.2` and `minimatch@9.0.5` instances are pinned by `eslint-config-next@15.2.2` and cannot be fixed via parent bumps without changing the Next.js tooling version. Targeted `pnpm.overrides` applied per-parent to force safe versions:

```json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "@eslint/config-array>minimatch": "^3.1.3",
    "eslint>minimatch": "^3.1.3",
    "eslint-plugin-import>minimatch": "^3.1.3",
    "eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y>minimatch": "^3.1.3",
    "eslint-plugin-react>minimatch": "^3.1.3",
    "@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree>minimatch": "^9.0.6"
  }
}
```

These overrides can be removed once `eslint-config-next` upgrades its bundled `@typescript-eslint` and `eslint-plugin-*` dependencies.

## Lockfile Verification

| Package | Before | After | Required |
|---------|--------|-------|----------|
| `minimatch` (v3) | `3.1.2` | `3.1.4` | `>= 3.1.3` ✅ |
| `minimatch` (v9) | `9.0.5` | `9.0.7` | `>= 9.0.6` ✅ |
| `playwright` | `1.52.0` | `1.58.2` | `>= 1.55.1` ✅ |
| `@langchain/core` | `1.0.2` | `1.1.28` | `>= 1.1.8` ✅ |
| `tar` | `7.4.3` | *(removed)* | removed ✅ |

author: echovic
body:
## Problem When using `feishu_doc` with `action: "append"` or `action: "write"`, blocks appear in random order instead of the order specified in the Markdown content. Fixes #26022 ## Root Cause `documentBlockChildren.create` batch API does not guarantee insertion order when multiple blocks are sent in a single call. Feishu processes the batch asynchronously, resulting in non-deterministic block positions. ## Fix Switch from batch insertion (all blocks in one API call) to sequential single-block inserts. Each block is appended one at a time, preserving the source markdown order. ## Changes - `extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts`: Replace batch `insertBlocks` with sequential per-block insertion - `extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts`: Add test verifying sequential insertion order ## Testing - Existing test passes (image fetch hardening) - New test verifies: 3 blocks → 3 sequential API calls, each with exactly 1 block in correct order

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes block insertion order in Feishu documents by switching from batch API insertion to sequential single-block inserts. The batch API (`documentBlockChildren.create` with multiple children) processes blocks asynchronously without guaranteed ordering. The fix inserts blocks one at a time, appending each to the end, which produces deterministic results that match the source markdown order. The implementation is straightforward: - Replaced single batch API call with a loop that makes one API call per block - Added clear inline comments explaining why sequential insertion is necessary - Added comprehensive test coverage verifying the sequential behavior - Error handling remains intact (throws on first failure)

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge with one minor consideration around partial failures - The fix correctly addresses the ordering issue with a well-tested solution. However, there's a potential edge case: if insertion fails mid-sequence, the document will be left in a partially-inserted state (some blocks added, others not), whereas the batch approach would be all-or-nothing. This is a minor trade-off for correctness, but worth noting for production scenarios with large documents. - No files require special attention Last reviewed commit: 276b393

This commit adds Nexus test case 9.2.14 which verifies that the DUT properly accepts and processes PAN ID Query requests and responds when a conflict is found.

Implementation details:
- tests/nexus/test_9_2_14.cpp: C++ test execution logic. Implements a 4-node topology (Leader_1, Router_1, Commissioner, Leader_2). Leader_2 forms a separate network on a secondary channel with the same PAN ID. Test uses direct core method calls and sets log level to note.
- tests/nexus/verify_9_2_14.py: Python pcap verification script. Verifies MGMT_PANID_QUERY requests (unicast and multicast) from the Commissioner and MGMT_PANID_CONFLICT responses from Router_1. Ensures correct TLVs are present in CoAP payloads.
- tests/nexus/CMakeLists.txt: Added nexus_9_2_14 target.
- tests/nexus/run_nexus_tests.sh: Added 9_2_14 to default test list.

body:
Automated: Migrate {target_path} from gsutil to gcloud storage

This CL is part of the on going effort to migrate from the legacy `gsutil` tool to the new and improved `gcloud storage` command-line interface.
`gcloud storage` is the recommended and modern tool for interacting with Google Cloud Storage, offering better performance, unified authentication, and a more consistent command structure with other `gcloud` components. 🚀

### Automation Details

This change was **generated automatically** by an agent that targets users of `gsutil`.
The transformations applied are based on the  [gsutil to gcloud storage migration guide](http://go/gsutil-gcloud-storage-migration-guide).

### ⚠️ Action Required: Please Review and Test Carefully

While we have based the automation on the migration guide, every use case is unique.
**It is crucial that you thoroughly test these changes in environments appropriate to your use-case before merging.**  
Be aware of potential differences between `gsutil` and `gcloud storage` that could impact your workflows.  
For instance, the structure of command output may have changed, requiring updates to any scripts that parse it. Similarly, command behavior can differ subtly; the `gcloud storage rsync` command has a different file deletion logic than `gsutil rsync`, which could lead to unintended file deletions.  

Our migration guides can help guide you through a list of mappings and some notable differences between the two tools.

Standard presubmit tests are run as part of this CL's workflow. **If you need to target an additional test workflow or require assistance with testing, please let us know.**

Please verify that all your Cloud Storage operations continue to work as expected to avoid any potential disruptions in production.

### Support and Collaboration

The `GCS CLI` team is here to help! If you encounter any issues, have a complex use case that this automated change doesn't cover, or face any other blockers, please don't hesitate to reach out.
We are happy to work with you to test and adjust these changes as needed.

**Contact:** `gcs-cli-hyd@google.com`

We appreciate your partnership in this important migration effort!

author: copilot
body:
Adds three missing scripts to bootstrap the ANSYS Copilot RAG pipeline end-to-end, replacing corrupted copy-paste versions with clean, syntax-validated files.

## New Scripts

- **`scripts/create_starter_knowledge.py`** — Generates `backend/knowledge_base/data/starter_knowledge.json` with 7 curated ANSYS reference documents (element types, material properties, convergence troubleshooting, mesh best practices, APDL command reference, analysis setup guides, PyMAPDL quick start). Content built via string concatenation to avoid triple-quote/encoding issues on Windows.

- **`scripts/build_starter_vectordb.py`** — Loads the knowledge JSON, chunks with `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=1000, overlap=200)`, embeds via `text-embedding-3-small`, and persists to ChromaDB (`ansys_knowledge` collection). Runs 5 retrieval test queries on completion.

- **`scripts/test_first_query.py`** — Loads the persisted vector store, builds a `RetrievalQA` chain (stuff, k=4) backed by an ANSYS Copilot expert system prompt, and runs 3 end-to-end test queries covering APDL code generation, convergence debugging, and PyMAPDL usage.

## Usage

```bash
python scripts/create_starter_knowledge.py   # writes starter_knowledge.json
python scripts/build_starter_vectordb.py     # embeds + persists to chroma_db/
python scripts/test_first_query.py           # full RAG pipeline smoke test
```

All scripts use `load_dotenv()` + `os.getenv()` with defaults matching `.env.example`. No new dependencies — all required packages (`langchain`, `langchain-openai`, `langchain-community`, `chromadb`, `openai`, `python-dotenv`) were already in `requirements.txt`.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ## Problem
> The user needs 3 working Python scripts added to the `scripts/` directory. These scripts were previously provided via chat but copy-paste into Notepad caused syntax errors (unterminated triple-quoted strings, encoding issues). We need clean, properly formatted versions pushed directly.
> 
> ## Scripts to Add/Replace
> 
> ### 1. `scripts/create_starter_knowledge.py`
> Creates a starter ANSYS knowledge base with 7 essential documents covering:
> - Common ANSYS element types (SOLID185, SOLID186, SOLID187, SHELL181, SHELL281, BEAM188, BEAM189, SOLID70, SOLID90, CONTA174, TARGET170) with descriptions, nodes, DOFs, best use cases, KEYOPTs
> - Common engineering material properties (Steel A36, Aluminum 6061-T6, Copper, Titanium Ti-6Al-4V) with APDL commands and unit system guidance
> - Convergence troubleshooting guide (substep size, element distortion, contact issues, material model issues, boundary conditions, large deformation, recommended solver settings, debugging steps)
> - Mesh best practices (general guidelines, mesh convergence study procedure, structural meshing, CFD meshing with y+ guidance, common APDL meshing commands)
> - Most used APDL commands reference (geometry, boolean ops, element types & material, meshing, analysis types, boundary conditions, loads, selection commands, solving, postprocessing)
> - Analysis type setup guides (static structural, modal, thermal steady-state, thermal-structural coupled, buckling, harmonic)
> - PyMAPDL quick start guide (installation, basic usage example, key methods, result extraction)
> 
> The script should:
> - Create `backend/knowledge_base/data/` directory if it doesn't exist
> - Store all 7 documents as a JSON list in `backend/knowledge_base/data/starter_knowledge.json`
> - Each document has: id, title, content (as a string with markdown formatting)
> - Print summary of created documents
> 
> ### 2. `scripts/build_starter_vectordb.py`
> Builds a ChromaDB vector database from the starter knowledge:
> - Load knowledge docs from `backend/knowledge_base/data/starter_knowledge.json`
> - Chunk using `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` (chunk_size=1000, chunk_overlap=200, separators=["\n## ", "\n### ", "\n\n", "\n", " "])
> - Create LangChain `Document` objects with metadata (source, title, chunk_index)
> - Generate embeddings using OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (from env var EMBEDDING_MODEL)
> - Store in ChromaDB with collection name "ansys_knowledge" and persist to CHROMA_PERSIST_DIR
> - Run 5 test queries to verify retrieval:
>   1. "What element should I use for a 3D structural analysis?"
>   2. "My nonlinear analysis won't converge, what should I do?"
>   3. "What are the material properties of steel in ANSYS?"
>   4. "How do I set up a modal analysis in APDL?"
>   5. "How do I use PyMAPDL to run a simulation?"
> - Print results summary with top result source and preview
> 
> Dependencies: `python-dotenv`, `langchain`, `langchain-openai`, `langchain-community`, `chromadb`
> 
> ### 3. `scripts/test_first_query.py`
> Tests the full RAG pipeline (retrieve + generate):
> - Load ChromaDB vector store
> - Set up ChatOpenAI LLM (model from MODEL_NAME env var, temperature from TEMPERATURE, max_tokens from MAX_TOKENS)
> - Create an ANSYS expert system prompt template that positions the AI as "ANSYS Copilot" expert
> - Build a LangChain RetrievalQA chain (stuff chain type, k=4 retrieval)
> - Run 3 test queries:
>   1. "Generate APDL code for a static structural analysis of a steel cantilever beam (100mm x 10mm x 10mm) with a 500N tip load"
>   2. "My nonlinear contact analysis won't converge. I'm using SOLID185 elements with large deformation. What should I check?"
>   3. "Write PyMAPDL code to run a modal analysis of an aluminum plate and extract the first 5 natural frequencies"
> - Print full AI responses with source documents used
> 
> Dependencies: same as build_starter_vectordb.py plus `openai`
> 
> ## Important Notes
> - All scripts must use `from dotenv import load_dotenv` and call `load_dotenv()` where env vars are needed
> - Use `os.getenv()` for all config values with sensible defaults
> - Scripts must work on Windows (the user is on Windows PowerShell)
> - Use UTF-8 encoding when writing files
> - All triple-quoted strings must be properly terminated
> - Keep the knowledge content comprehensive but ensure all strings are properly escaped
> - The existing files in scripts/ (build_vectordb.py, process_data.py, scrape_ansys_docs.py) should NOT be modified
> - Also update requirements.txt to ensure python-dotenv and all needed packages are listed
>

author: kaizhou-lab
body:
## Summary

Fixes #971 — Windows installer installs but `AionUi.exe` is missing, leaving only uninstaller and desktop shortcut.

**Root cause:** Two issues introduced in #947 (build system migration):

1. **`ELECTRON_BUILDER_COMPRESSION_LEVEL` set to `'maximum'` (string)**
   - 7za's `-mx` flag only accepts numeric values (0–9)
   - `-mx=maximum` caused `E_INVALIDARG` / "The parameter is incorrect" errors
   - This was misdiagnosed as "7za fails on large dirs"

2. **7zip-bin monkey-patch masked the real error**
   - The patch replaced all `7za.exe` calls with PowerShell `ZipFile::CreateFromDirectory` on Windows
   - This hid the `-mx=maximum` bug (PowerShell ignores 7za args)
   - But PowerShell only creates ZIP format, not 7z — NSIS's `nsis7z.dll` cannot extract ZIP archives
   - Result: installer stub fails to extract app files silently

**Fix:**
- Remove the Windows `child_process.spawn/execFile` monkey-patch from 7zip-bin patch (keep macOS symlink wrapper)
- Fix compression level: `'maximum'`/`'normal'` → `'9'`/`'7'`

**Verified:** CI build produces 165 MB installer (was 235 MB), `app-64.7z` is real 7z format (`LZMA2` compression).

## Changes
- `patches/7zip-bin@5.2.0.patch` — remove Windows monkey-patch, keep macOS wrapper
- `scripts/build-with-builder.js` — fix `ELECTRON_BUILDER_COMPRESSION_LEVEL` to numeric values

## Test plan
- [x] CI build succeeds on Windows
- [x] NSIS installer `app-64.7z` verified as real 7z format (not ZIP)
- [x] Installer size reduced from 235 MB to 165 MB (proper 7z compression)
- [ ] Install on Windows and verify `AionUi.exe` exists

Closes #971

body:
### Motivation

- Introduce explicit runtime separation between ambient and reactive NPC flows and provide extension points for cluster/LOD orchestration.
- Add lightweight cluster-level lifecycle orchestration to manage area RUNNING/PAUSED/STOPPED transitions with grace windows, caps and rate-limiting.
- Provide a baseline hidden/projected LOD pipeline for ambient NPCs to drastically reduce cost for non-interest areas and enable deterministic fast-forward/resync on reveal.

### Description

- Added new runtime mode helpers in `src/modules/npc/npc_runtime_modes_inc.nss` to support `ambient`/`reactive` layers, dispatch modes, cluster owner and interest state, and NPC LOD/projected state APIs.
- Implemented cluster lifecycle supervisor in `src/modules/npc/npc_cluster_supervisor_inc.nss` to resolve cluster owners, enforce grace window policy, interior soft/hard caps, and a token-bucket transition rate limiter with metrics emission.
- Implemented LOD/projection baseline in `src/modules/npc/npc_lod_projection_inc.nss` providing hiding/reveal logic, projection capture, fast-forwarding of waypoint progress, and per-NPC simulation LOD state (`FULL`, `REDUCED`, `PROJECTED`).
- Integrated the new subsystems into core flows by updating `npc_core.nss` to include new headers and forward-declaring new APIs, and by modifying `npc_lifecycle_inc.nss` to apply LOD on area state changes, call cluster orchestration during maintenance/bootstrap, and to call cluster enter/exit handlers on area player count changes.
- Adjusted tick/dispatch behavior to split ambient (idle fan-out) and reactive (queued event) processing: gating idle fan-out with `NpcBhvrAreaAllowsAmbientDispatch` and gating reactive queue processing with `NpcBhvrAreaAllowsReactiveDispatch`, and updated tick-state commit and metrics logic accordingly.
- Modified NPC event handlers to respect runtime-layer and area dispatch mode: `NpcBhvrResolveNpcLayer` / `NpcBhvrNpcUsesReactivePath` checks on `OnPerception`, `OnDamaged`, and `OnDialogue`, and LOD-aware idle skipping using `NpcBhvrLodShouldSkipIdleTick` in `npc_activity_inc.nss`.
- Added LOD/cluster metrics and new metric keys in `npc_metrics_inc.nss` and updated various helpers (e.g. `NpcBhvrMetricAdd` usage) to support incremental metrics and cluster/LOD observability.
- Small API and behavior tweaks: `NpcBhvrActivityApplyRouteState` declaration, minor local variable writes, and lifecycle helper calls on spawn to resolve NPC layer and apply initial LOD.
- Documentation (`src/modules/npc/README.md`) updated to describe the new runtime mode split, cluster orchestration (Phase B), and LOD projection (Phase C) with configuration keys and metrics listed.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this change; follow the updated module README to run the recommended checks, for example `bash scripts/test_npc_smoke.sh`, `bash scripts/check_npc_lifecycle_contract.sh`, and `bash scripts/check_npc_legacy_compat_contract.sh`.

author: roasbeef
body:
In this PR, we fix a gap in the durable actor framework's atomicity
guarantee by teaching `TransactionExecutor.ExecTx` to respect the outer
database transaction that `TxAwareActorDeliveryStore` injects into the
context via `actor.WithTx`.

Previously, every call to `ExecTx` unconditionally created a new database
transaction via `BeginTx`, even when the context already carried one from
the actor framework. This meant that inner stores (e.g., `PackageStore`,
`VTXOStore`) each ran in their own isolated transactions rather than
participating in the actor's per-message transaction. A crash between any
two of these inner transactions would leave the store in an inconsistent
state: a package persisted but its bindings lost, or an FSM state advanced
but the outgoing artifacts never written.

The fix is a small early-return at the top of `ExecTx`: we check
`actor.TxFromContext(ctx)` and, when present, pass the existing `*sql.Tx`
directly to `createQuery`, bypassing the retry loop entirely (the outer
transaction owner handles retries and commit/rollback). When no outer
transaction is present, existing behavior is preserved unchanged.

## Tests

Four new tests in `db/tx_executor_ctx_test.go` verify the behavior:

`TestExecTx_JoinOuterActorTx` confirms that writes through `ExecTx` land
in the outer transaction and aren't visible globally until the outer tx
commits. `TestExecTx_StandaloneNoTx` is the regression test for the
existing standalone path. `TestExecTx_OuterTxRollbackAtomicity` exercises
the key invariant: two sequential `ExecTx` calls joining the same outer
transaction are both discarded atomically on rollback. Finally,
`TestExecTx_OuterTxErrorPropagation` verifies that errors from `txBody`
propagate cleanly without touching the outer transaction's lifecycle.

See each commit message for a detailed description w.r.t the incremental
changes.

body:
The mirror workflow only supported WeChat Work (企业微信) notifications. This adds parallel Telegram notification support via the Bot API.

## Changes

- **`jobs.build.env`**: Added `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` mapped from repository secrets
- **New step `telegram send message`**: Fires after the WeChat step, gated on both secrets being present; sends a plain-text `curl` POST to the Telegram Bot API with the same `IMAGE_URL` format used by the WeChat step

```yaml
- name: telegram send message
  if: ${{ env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN != '' && env.TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID != '' }}
  env:
    IMAGE_URL: ${{ github.event.inputs.TARGET_REGISTRY }}/${{ github.event.inputs.TARGET_REPOSITORY }}/${{ github.event.inputs.NEW_NAME }}:${{ github.event.inputs.IMAGE_VERSION }}
  run: |
    curl -s -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}/sendMessage" \
      -d chat_id="${TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID}" \
      -d text="镜像同步成功: ${{ env.IMAGE_URL }}"
```

Existing WeChat behavior is unchanged; Telegram notifications are entirely opt-in via secrets.

author: vimalprakashts
body:
## Summary

- **Data corruption bug**: `IN(subquery)` returns `1` instead of `NULL` in ungrouped aggregate queries where no rows match the `WHERE` clause, when the LHS column is declared `NOT NULL`
- Wrong values are physically stored via `INSERT...SELECT`, corrupting persistent data
- Root cause: the IN expression compiler skipped the `IsNull` check when the LHS column was `NOT NULL`, but `NullRow` (used in ungrouped aggregates with no matching rows) overrides all column values to NULL regardless of constraints
- Fix: always emit `IsNull` before `NotFound`/`Found` in IN expressions

## Reproducer

```sql
CREATE TABLE src(a TEXT PRIMARY KEY, val REAL NOT NULL, flag INTEGER);
INSERT INTO src VALUES (NULL, 1.5, NULL);

-- Query returns 1|NULL instead of NULL|NULL
SELECT val IN (SELECT a FROM src), AVG(1) FROM src WHERE flag >= 99;

-- Wrong value gets stored (data corruption)
CREATE TABLE dst(in_result, agg_result);
INSERT INTO dst SELECT val IN (SELECT a FROM src), AVG(1) FROM src WHERE flag >= 99;
SELECT in_result, typeof(in_result) FROM dst;
-- SQLite: NULL|null
-- Turso (before fix): 1|integer
```

## Simulator gap

`IN(subquery)` expression generation is commented out in `sql_generation/generation/expr.rs` line 177:
```rust
// TODO: skip InSelect as still need to implement ArbitratyFrom for Select
```

The differential fuzzer (which does generate IN subqueries) found this bug with seed `16648648351493581373`.

## Test plan

- [x] 3 new regression tests in `testing/runner/tests/in-subquery-ungrouped-aggregate.sqltest` (all pass)
- [x] Full sqltest suite: 6896 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Core unit tests: 1339 passed
- [x] `cargo clippy` clean
- [x] Updated 3 bytecode snapshot tests

author: bezhermoso
body:
## Summary

The installer's `configure_shell_rc()` hardcoded `$HOME/.zshrc` and `$HOME/.bashrc` as the only rc files to configure. This silently did nothing (no snippet appended, no warning shown) in two common scenarios:

1. **`ZDOTDIR` is set** — zsh reads `$ZDOTDIR/.zshrc`, not `$HOME/.zshrc`. This is common with dotfile managers (chezmoi, stow, yadm) and users who keep `$HOME` clean via XDG-style layouts.
2. **macOS Bash with only `.bash_profile`** — macOS Terminal.app and iTerm2 open login shells by default, which source `~/.bash_profile`, not `~/.bashrc`. Users without a `.bashrc` were silently skipped.

### Changes

**`install.sh` — `configure_shell_rc()`**
- Zsh detection now respects `ZDOTDIR`: checks `${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zshrc`
- Bash detection falls back from `.bashrc` to `.bash_profile` (first existing file wins)
- Emits a `warn` when no rc file is found at all, with the exact line to add manually

**`install.sh` — Legacy migration loop**
- The `for rc_file in ...` loop that migrates `.config/wt` → `.wt` references now checks the same expanded set of paths: `${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zshrc`, `$HOME/.bashrc`, `$HOME/.bash_profile`
- When `ZDOTDIR` is unset, the first and second entries both resolve under `$HOME`; the `grep` guard prevents double-processing

**`install.sh` — Post-install banner**
- The "Reload your shell" instruction now dynamically shows the correct file path instead of the hardcoded `source ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc`
- Replaces `$HOME` prefix with `~` for a clean display

**`wt.sh` — `_wt_ensure_sourced()` error messages**
- Zsh block: `~/.zshrc` → `${ZDOTDIR:-~}/.zshrc`
- Bash block: `~/.bashrc` → `~/.bashrc (or ~/.bash_profile)`

## Test plan

- [x] `./test/bats/bin/bats test/unit/ test/integration/ test/e2e/` — 167/168 pass (1 pre-existing failure in `wt-remove --merged` unrelated to this change)
- [x] Manual: set `ZDOTDIR` to a temp dir containing a `.zshrc`, run installer, verify snippet lands in the correct file
- [x] Manual: on macOS with only `~/.bash_profile` (no `~/.bashrc`), run installer, verify snippet lands in `.bash_profile`
- [x] Manual: with neither rc file present, verify warning is printed

author: copilot
body:
Several hot paths were issuing redundant or unbounded queries — most critically, `ConsistencyTracker` re-ran expensive aggregations it had just computed, a per-week loop re-queried habits from the DB on every iteration, and the task creation form fetched every book/habit in the system regardless of user.

## Database indexes
New migration adds composite indexes on the column pairs that appear together in `WHERE` clauses across the codebase. Without them every filtered query does a full table scan.

| Table | Indexes added |
|---|---|
| `books` | `(user_id, is_completed)`, `(user_id, updated_at)`, `(user_id, genre)` |
| `habits` | `(user_id, is_active)`, `(user_id, last_completed)` |
| `tasks` | `(user_id, is_completed)`, `(user_id, updated_at)`, `(user_id, due_date)` |
| `journals` | `(user_id, entry_date)` |
| `habit_completions` | `(habit_id, completed_at)` |

## Eliminated duplicate queries in `ConsistencyTracker`
`calculateOverallConsistencyScore()` was re-executing `calculateHabitConsistency()` and `calculateTaskCompletionRate()` even though `getUserConsistencyMetrics()` had just called them. Results are now computed once and reused:

```php
// Before – 4 DB round-trips total
return [
    'habit_consistency'  => $this->calculateHabitConsistency(…),   // query 1
    'task_completion_rate' => $this->calculateTaskCompletionRate(…), // query 2
    'consistency_score'  => $this->calculateOverallConsistencyScore(…), // queries 3 & 4
];

// After – 2 DB round-trips, score derived from already-fetched data
$habitConsistency   = $this->calculateHabitConsistency(…);
$taskCompletionRate = $this->calculateTaskCompletionRate(…);
$consistencyScore   = /* weighted avg computed in-memory */;
```

## Fixed N+1 habit queries in `calculateGrowthTrends()`
`calculateWeeklyHabitConsistency()` was called inside a per-week loop and re-queried `habits` on every iteration. Habits are now loaded once before the loop and passed as a `Collection`.

## Fixed `getHabitCompletionDays()` — wrong data source and O(n) loop
The method iterated day-by-day comparing against the single `last_completed` field, meaning at most one day could ever register as completed across any date range. Replaced with a single query against the `habit_completions` table (which exists for this purpose). The same fix is applied to the 30-day calendar in `HabitController::show()`.

## `AnalyticsController` — 3 COUNT queries → 1
```php
// Before
'total'      => Book::where('user_id', $userId)->count(),
'completed'  => Book::where('user_id', $userId)->where('is_completed', true)->count(),
'in_progress'=> Book::where('user_id', $userId)->where('is_completed', false)->count(),

// After
$bookCounts = Book::where('user_id', $userId)
    ->selectRaw('COUNT(*) as total, SUM(…) as completed, SUM(…) as in_progress')
    ->first();
```

## `TaskController::create()` — unscoped `Book::all()` / `Habit::all()`
Both calls fetched every row in the table without a user filter, leaking other users' data into the form and loading unbounded result sets. Replaced with user-scoped, column-projected queries.

- Hard-money loans are typically charged on the purchase amount rather than the financed balance, so interest calculations should reflect the purchase/offer price for accurate cost estimates.

author: l3enjamin
body:
The goal of this task was to replace blocking I/O calls in `scripts/run_skill.js` with non-blocking `fs.promises` equivalents.

Changes:
- In `scripts/run_skill.js`, `fs.existsSync` and `fs.readFileSync` were replaced with `fs.promises.access` and `fs.promises.readFile`.
- Since `run_skill.js` depends on `search_skills.js`, the latter was also refactored to be asynchronous.
- `search_skills.js` now uses `Promise.all` to load skill metadata in parallel, which significantly improves efficiency when many skills are present.
- All functions are now correctly awaited in the `async` context.

Performance Impact:
- While wall-clock time for a single execution with few skills remains similar (with slight promise overhead), the architectural improvement prevents the Node.js event loop from being blocked.
- Parallel file reading in `searchSkills` provides a scalable performance boost as the number of skills grows.
- Verified functional correctness by running `run_skill.js` and confirmed successful skill loading and search.

author: pranavkonde
body:
This PR establishes the foundational API architecture for SplitFare. It introduces a standardized request/response lifecycle, middleware for security and validation, and a type-safe client for frontend integration.

### **Key Changes**

**Core API Utilities & Middleware**
- **[api-utils.ts](file:///Users/pranavkonde/Desktop/Projects/splitfare_storacha/lib/api-utils.ts)**: Centralized `withMiddleware` wrapper handling logging, error normalization, and higher-order protection.
- **[errors.ts](file:///Users/pranavkonde/Desktop/Projects/splitfare_storacha/lib/errors.ts)**: Custom `AppError` hierarchy for structured, client-friendly error responses.
- **Authentication**: `withAuth` middleware using `@privy-io/node` for secure JWT verification.
- **Validation**: `withValidation` middleware for schema enforcement using Zod.

**Security & Performance**
- **[rate-limit.ts](file:///Users/pranavkonde/Desktop/Projects/splitfare_storacha/lib/rate-limit.ts)**: Distributed rate limiting powered by Upstash Redis (10 req/10s window).
- **Logging**: Automatic capture of HTTP method, path, status, and execution duration for every request.

**Type Safety & Schemas**
- **[validations/index.ts](file:///Users/pranavkonde/Desktop/Projects/splitfare_storacha/lib/validations/index.ts)**: Comprehensive Zod schemas for `User`, `Group`, `Expense`, and `Settlement`.
- **[api-client.ts](file:///Users/pranavkonde/Desktop/Projects/splitfare_storacha/lib/api-client.ts)**: A singleton, typed fetch wrapper for frontend use, supporting automatic token injection.

**API Scaffolding**
- Initial route structures implemented for:
  - `GET /api/users/me`
  - `GET/POST /api/groups`
  - `GET/POST /api/expenses`
  - `GET/POST /api/settlements`

### **Acceptance Criteria Verification**
- [x] `withAuth()` rejects unauthenticated requests with 401.
- [x] `withValidation()` rejects invalid payloads with 400.
- [x] `AppError` produces structured JSON error responses.
- [x] Rate limiter blocks excessive requests with 429.
- [x] API client provides typed methods for all resources.
- [x] Zod schemas cover all core entities.
- [x] Logging captures method, path, status, and duration.
- [x] All routes return consistent `ApiResponse<T>` format.

### **Environment Variables Required**
```env
PRIVY_APP_ID=...
PRIVY_APP_SECRET=...
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=...
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=...
```

author: dmoerner
body:
## Description

The `<SignIn>` component can already be used in a sign-in-or-sign-up flow (`CombinedFlow`) under certain conditions. When strict enumeration protection is enabled, make that combined flow pass the `signUpIfMissing` parameter to the backend to allow an enumeration-safe combined flow. Previously, attempting to use a combined flow with strict enumeration protection enabled was silently broken.

Under the hood, the backend treats sign up if missing as an account transfer. We therefore add support for this account transfer logic when handling first factor verification in the combined sign in flow when strict enumeration protection is enabled.

Fixes USER-4769.

We should merge this in coordination with documentation and a Changelog release, since it will change existing behavior (although with a fix for something that is currently broken)

## Technical Implementation
- **Search Algorithm**: It simulates the game 4 turns ahead (d=4) to evaluate the best possible outcome while ignoring "bad" branches.
- **Evaluation Heuristic**: The game tree is too large to solve completely, so the bot scores based on:
  -  **Winning Conditions**: High priority given to pieces touching any of the three board edges.
  - **Connectivity**: Bonus priority if there are same-color neighbors.
  - **Defensive strategy**: The player's scores are multiplied by 1.2x, which makes the bot prioritize blocking moves over placing its own pieces.

## Other changes
- Adapted the original unit tests to ensure the AI respects board boundaries and handles the board correctly.

Closes #21

author: badvoidstar
body:
Eliminate self-echo for object updates
Object update broadcasts now use OthersInGroup instead of Group.
The sender gets version sync, member sequence tracking, and RTT from
the UpdateObjects response instead of an echoed broadcast. This:
- Reduces bandwidth (~50% fewer update messages in 2-player sessions)
- Provides more accurate RTT (request/response vs broadcast echo)
- Eliminates the isSelfEcho code path and version-only update logic

Skip gap detection for own member sequence
After eliminating self-echo, UpdateObjects tracks the sender's own
sequence via the await response while Create/Delete/Replace broadcast
to the sender synchronously. The broadcast callback can fire before
the await continuation (microtask boundary), causing false gaps.

Fix: only detect gaps for other members' streams. The sender can't
miss their own events since they initiated them. Own sequence is still
tracked to keep the memberSequences map current for reconciliation.

body:
`Dockerfile.supervised` build was failing because `deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x` exited with code 1. Also fixes a pnpm version drift (`10.24.0` vs `10.28.1` used everywhere else).

## Summary

Replace the unreliable nodesource apt install of Node.js 24 with a direct `COPY --from=builder` from the existing `node:24-bookworm-slim` builder stage. Eliminates the external runtime dependency and guarantees version consistency across stages.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change

## Related Issue

## Changes

- Replace `curl … deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | bash -` + `apt-get install nodejs` with `COPY --from=builder` of node binaries and node_modules
- Bump pnpm from `10.24.0` → `10.28.1` to match `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.timescale`

**Before:**
```dockerfile
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && corepack enable \
    && corepack prepare pnpm@10.24.0 --activate \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

**After:**
```dockerfile
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/bin/node /usr/local/bin/
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/bin/npm /usr/local/bin/
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/bin/npx /usr/local/bin/
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/bin/corepack /usr/local/bin/
COPY --from=builder /usr/local/lib/node_modules /usr/local/lib/node_modules/
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10.28.1 --activate
```

## Testing

- [ ] Added/updated unit tests
- [ ] Ran test suite locally (`pnpm test:unit`)
- [x] Tested manually

body:
## Summary
This PR implements API versioning for the Veritasor Backend, enabling future compatibility with multiple API versions. All routes are now mounted under `/api/v1` with middleware-based version tracking.

## Type of Change
- ✨ New feature

## Changes Made

### 1. New Middleware: `src/middleware/apiVersion.ts`
- **`apiVersionMiddleware`**: Extracts the API version from the request path (e.g., `/api/v1/...`) and attaches it to the request object as `req.apiVersion`
- **`versionResponseMiddleware`**: Adds an `API-Version` response header to all responses for client awareness

### 2. Updated: `src/index.ts`
- Imported versioning middleware functions
- Registered both middleware globally
- Updated route prefixes:
  - `/api/health` → `/api/v1/health`
  - `/api/attestations` → `/api/v1/attestations`

### 3. Updated: `README.md`
- Added "API Versioning" section explaining the approach
- Updated API endpoint table with `/api/v1` paths
- Documented how to extend for future versions (v2, v3, etc.)
- Included information about response headers

## Technical Details

### Versioning Strategy
- **Middleware-based**: Version extraction happens at the middleware level
- **Request-level tracking**: `req.apiVersion` can be accessed in route handlers
- **Response headers**: All responses include `API-Version: v1`
- **Extensible**: New versions can be added by creating new routes under `/api/v2`, `/api/v3`, etc.

### Current API Endpoints
```
GET  /api/v1/health          - Health check
GET  /api/v1/attestations    - List attestations (stub)
POST /api/v1/attestations    - Submit attestation (stub)
```

## Testing
✅ TypeScript compilation successful  
✅ No type errors  
✅ Dependencies installed  
✅ Build output verified  

## Breaking Changes
⚠️ **Yes** - All API clients must update their endpoints from `/api/*` to `/api/v1/*`

## Future Considerations
- When adding v2, create new routers and mount at `/api/v2/*`
- Current middleware automatically extracts version numbers, so no changes needed for new versions
- Consider adding version validation if specific versions need different behavior
- Could extend to deprecate old versions if needed

## Related Issues
Close #40 

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed the changes
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes
- [x] Updated documentation (README.md)
- [x] Changes generate no new warnings

# 📂 Issue: Optimierung und Bugfixes der Ordner-Logik

## 🎯 Ziel
Die Ordner-Erstellung und -Interaktion soll stabiler, intuitiver und konsistenter gestaltet werden.

Mehrere Logik-Anpassungen und Bugfixes sind notwendig.

---

## 🧩 User Story

Als Nutzer  
möchte ich Ordner sauber und ohne unerwartetes Verhalten erstellen und verwenden können,  
damit die Organisation meiner Apps zuverlässig und intuitiv funktioniert.

---

## 🔧 Anforderungen & Anpassungen

### 1️⃣ Direktes Auswahlmenü bei erster Ordner-Erstellung

**Aktuelles Verhalten:**  
Ordner wird zuerst erstellt, danach erfolgt die Bearbeitung.

**Neues Verhalten:**  
- Beim ersten Erstellen eines Ordners öffnet sich sofort das App-Auswahlmenü
- Der Ordner wird erst final erstellt, nachdem mindestens eine App ausgewählt wurde
- Falls der Vorgang abgebrochen wird → kein leerer Ordner wird erstellt

---

### 2️⃣ Keine doppelte App in einem Ordner

- Eine App, die sich bereits in einem Ordner befindet, darf nicht erneut auswählbar sein
- Die App soll im Auswahlmenü deaktiviert werden
- Keine doppelten Einträge innerhalb eines Ordners

---

### 3️⃣ Bugfix: Ziehen von rechts nach links

**Problem:**  
Beim Ziehen von rechts nach links tritt teilweise fehlerhaftes Verhalten auf.

**Ziel:**  
- Konsistentes Drag-Verhalten in beide Richtungen
- Kein Springen, kein unerwartetes Zurücksetzen
- Gleichmäßige Animation

---

### 4️⃣ Kein Scrollen ohne Inhalt

**Problem:**

author: sokra
body:
### What?

Replaces the vendored `jest-worker` dependency with a purpose-built worker pool implementation (`packages/next/src/lib/worker/`). Deletes the compiled `jest-worker` bundle and all associated type declarations.

### Why?

- `jest-worker` is maintained for Jest's needs, not Next.js's. It eagerly spawns all workers at construction and doesn't support per-worker concurrency, boot throttling, or fine-grained crash recovery.
- Removing it eliminates a compiled dependency that was difficult to debug and upgrade.
- A custom pool lets us add features like lazy spawning and boot throttling that directly benefit `next build` performance with many static pages.

### How?

**New files in `packages/next/src/lib/worker/`:**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `worker-pool.ts` | Core pool: lazy spawning, dynamic scaling, per-worker concurrency, task queue, crash recovery, graceful shutdown |
| `index.ts` | High-level `Worker` class (drop-in replacement): timeout/restart, NODE_OPTIONS, color propagation, exposed methods |
| `types.ts` | Shared message constants and TypeScript types for the IPC protocol |
| `worker-child-common.ts` | Shared child protocol logic (`ChildTransport` + `createMessageHandler`) |
| `worker-process-child.ts` | `child_process` entry point (thin wrapper) |
| `worker-thread-child.ts` | `worker_threads` entry point (thin wrapper) |
| `README.md` | Architecture docs, message protocol, complete options/methods reference |

**Key features of the new pool:**

- **Lazy spawning**: Workers are created on-demand when tasks are dispatched, not at construction time
- **Dynamic scaling**: Worker count grows from 0 to `maxWorkers` as concurrent tasks increase
- **Per-worker concurrency**: `concurrencyPerWorker` allows multiple in-flight calls per worker
- **Boot throttling**: `maxBootingWorkers` (default: `ceil(maxWorkers/4)`) limits concurrent worker startups. Workers send a `PARENT_MESSAGE_READY` message after loading their module and running `setup()`. When the booting limit is reached, tasks queue instead of spawning new workers.
- **Fault recovery**: `maxRespawns` controls how many times a worker slot is respawned after unexpected exits. In-flight requests are always rejected; queued tasks are dispatched to healthy workers.

**Other changes:**

- `collect-build-traces.ts`: Updated standalone trace paths from `jest-worker/*Child` to `worker-*-child`
- `type-check.ts`: Removed stale `'Call retries were exceeded'` catch guard (jest-worker message that the new pool never produces), removed unnecessary try/catch wrapper
- `next-dev-server.ts`: Switched import to new `Worker` class, added required options (`debuggerPortOffset`, `isolatedMemory`, `exposedMethods`), removed manual stdout/stderr piping (handled internally now)
- `tsec-exemptions.json`: Added `ban-eval-calls` exemption for `worker-child-common.ts` (`eval('require')` prevents static analysis of dynamic module paths in child process entry points)
- `errors.json`: Added error codes 1076–1085 for worker pool error messages
- Deleted `src/compiled/jest-worker/` and removed type declarations from `compiled.d.ts` / `$$compiled.internal.d.ts`

**Updated existing tests:**

- `test/production/next-server-nft`: Updated NFT snapshot to include 6 new `dist/lib/worker/*.js` files
- `test/e2e/cpu-profiling`: Updated expected CPU profile counts (+1 for `build-static-worker` profile)

**New test coverage:**

- `worker-pool.test.ts`: 55 tests covering lazy spawning, initialization, dispatch/message handling, task queuing, concurrency, custom messages, end/close, worker exit handling, stdout/stderr, dynamic scaling, fork options, respawning, maxBootingWorkers (throttling, READY signaling, crash recovery, setup error recovery, validation, shutdown)
- `worker.test.ts`: 41 tests covering the high-level Worker class (color propagation, option passthrough, exposed methods, end/close lifecycle, env configuration, timeout/activity, exit handler cleanup)

author: overlookmotel
body:
Refactor.

Previously we converted spans from UTF-8 to UTF-16 in AST first, then serialized tokens. This meant that when serializing tokens, we had to convert spans to UTF-16 before comparing offsets of overrides to the token's start offset (because the override offsets are taken from the AST nodes during the AST walk pass).

Instead, convert token spans first, *then* the AST. This removes span conversion from the critical path. On a CPU with instruction-level parallelism, other work can start without being blocked on waiting for the result of span conversion, and the two can happen in parallel.

This should be a slight perf improvement, though it likely won't show up on CodSpeed benchmarks as CodSpeed's CPU simulation to basic to emulate instruction-level parallelism.

But mainly, the motivation is that this makes the process simpler and easier to reason about.

author: copilot
body:
The built `.component` was silently rejected by Logic Pro due to a bundle identifier mismatch between the compiled binary and the bundle's `Info.plist`, compounded by a stale `JuceHeader.h` and no guidance that Projucer must be re-run before every Xcode build.

## Root causes

- **XCODE_MAC export used a placeholder bundle ID** (`com.yourcompany.straDellaMIDI_plugin`). Projucer's export-level `bundleIdentifier` overrides the project-level value when generating the Xcode build settings, so the built `Info.plist` had a different `CFBundleIdentifier` than what the compiled binary registered with the AU system → Logic silently failed validation.

- **`JuceLibraryCode/JuceHeader.h` included removed modules** — `juce_audio_formats` and `juce_audio_utils` were removed from the `.jucer` in a prior session but `JuceHeader.h` was never updated to match, leaving the committed file inconsistent with what Projucer would regenerate.

- **`Builds/` is gitignored** — without an explicit warning, users rebuild in Xcode against the stale pre-pull Xcode project, which still carries the wrong bundle ID regardless of `.jucer` or `JucePluginDefines.h` changes.

## Changes

- **`straDellaMIDI_plugin.jucer`** — corrected `XCODE_MAC bundleIdentifier` to `net.papacoyote.straDellaMIDI_plugin`, aligning the generated Info.plist with `JucePlugin_CFBundleIdentifier`.

- **`JuceLibraryCode/JuceHeader.h`** — removed stale `#include` lines for `juce_audio_formats` and `juce_audio_utils`; list now exactly matches the eleven modules declared in the `.jucer`.

- **`README.md`**
  - Added macOS 11+ requirement (`kAudioUnitType_MIDIProcessor` / `aump` is only recognized by the OS at runtime on macOS 11+).
  - Added prominent build warning: Projucer *must* be re-saved before every Xcode build so the regenerated Xcode project picks up the correct bundle ID and AU type.
  - Added `auval -v aump Vb4d Manu` as a mandatory pre-Logic validation step.
  - Added both AU cache paths to clear after rebuild, Logic Plug-in Manager rescan steps, and a Gatekeeper `xattr` command for components copied from another machine.

body:
### Proposed Changes

Added correct handling for sub-process annotations during collapse/expand, copy/paste, and remove actions. 

The root cause of this behavior is that 'Text Annotations' are placed at the `bpmn:process` level rather than inside the `bpmn:subProcess`. While they appear visually inside, they are not included in `element.children`. Consequently, copy/paste and collapse operations lose them because these operations are intended to work only with children. 

Based on the possible solution options [discussion](https://github.com/camunda/camunda-modeler/issues/5163#issuecomment-3946571271), manual handling for annotations was implemented for sub-process actions. Additionally, nested sub-processes were addressed by ensuring annotations are processed recursively across all levels.

author: schmalle
body:
Fixes multiple issues causing first-time OAuth users to get errors
(clearing cookies/private mode worked as a workaround):

1. Clear stale secman_auth HttpOnly cookie at OAuth flow start
   - Frontend JS cannot clear HttpOnly cookies, so the /authorize
     endpoint now sends a logout cookie on redirect
   - Prevents stale cookies from shared browsers or failed prior
     attempts from interfering with the callback

2. Use case-insensitive email lookup (findByEmailIgnoreCase)
   - Azure AD may return emails in varying cases across sessions
   - Prevents duplicate user creation from case mismatches

3. Handle username collisions during OAuth user creation
   - If email-prefix username already exists, append numeric suffix
   - Prevents ConstraintViolationException when local users share
     the same email prefix as new OAuth users

4. Use REQUIRES_NEW transaction for user creation
   - createNewOidcUser now commits independently of handleCallback
   - Prevents user creation rollback if later steps fail (e.g.,
     lastLogin update), which caused "works on second try" behavior

5. Wrap lastLogin update in try/catch
   - Prevents non-critical lastLogin failure from rolling back
     the entire OAuth callback transaction

6. Comprehensive OAuth flow logging with correlation IDs
   - Every step logged with [correlationId] prefix for tracing
   - Stale cookie detection logged at authorize and callback
   - User find/create operations logged with full context
   - Error paths log specific exception types and messages

### Motivation
- Rebrand the product to "Nethgram" and enhance the gifting UX with animated Lottie assets and richer UI components. 
- Improve real-time behavior by making websocket presence updates and message delivery more consistent between HTTP and WS flows. 
- Modernize frontend visuals and dialogs, and provide admin-only gift controls and supply tracking for collectible gifts.

### Description
- Rebranded app strings and titles across the codebase from `CL`/`CL Messenger` to `Nethgram` and updated various UI logos and copy.

- Added `PROJECT_ANALYSIS.md` with a project audit/plan and updated `frontend/src/mockData.js` to include the new gift definitions.

author: copilot
body:
Kalshi's authentication rejects requests when the signature is computed over a truncated path. The signed string must use the full path (e.g. `/trade-api/v2/events`), not the short resource path (`/events`), and must exclude query parameters.

## What changed

### `clients/kalshi_client.py` — `_sign`
- **Prepend base path**: extract the path component from `config.kalshi_base_url` via `urlparse` and prepend it so the signed string uses `/trade-api/v2/<resource>` as Kalshi requires
- **Strip query parameters**: split on `?` before constructing the message to sign — query params are passed separately to httpx and must never appear in the signature

```python
# Before — signs "/events" (wrong path, 401 on every request)
msg = (ts + method.upper() + path).encode()

# After — signs "/trade-api/v2/events" with no query string
path_no_query = path.split("?")[0]
base_path = urlparse(config.kalshi_base_url).path.rstrip("/")
full_path = base_path + path_no_query
msg = (ts + method.upper() + full_path).encode()
```

### `tests/test_kalshi_client.py` — `TestSign`
Added four tests covering:
- Query string absent from signed message when path contains `?`
- Signed message contains `/trade-api/v2/events`, not bare `/events`
- Combined path prefix + query-stripping behaviour
- `KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP` is in milliseconds (13-digit integer)

author: v7ncentng
body:
# Add attention score extraction module (`attention_extraction.py`)

This PR introduces `attention_extraction.py`, which implements Step 6 of the LeanCode
pipeline. This is responsible for extracting per-token attention scores from
fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 models over the CodeSearchNet Java dataset and
aggregating them into the category-local averages that drive the simplification algorithm.

---

## Module Structure

### Model Loading — `load_codebert()`, `load_codet5()`

Load the fine-tuned tokenizer and model onto the target device with
`output_attentions=True`. That flag is required to instruct PyTorch to retain attention
weight tensors in memory during the forward pass — without it there is nothing to
extract. Models are set to `.eval()` to disable dropout and ensure deterministic scores.

### AST Category Alignment — `_build_word_offsets()`, `map_subword_tokens_to_categories()`

The model operates on subword tokens (e.g. `bubble` → `["bub", "##ble"]`) but the
simplification algorithm needs to know which AST statement category each token belongs
to (`Method Signature`, `Return`, `For`, etc.). These two functions bridge that gap.

`_build_word_offsets()` takes the `(word, category)` pairs returned by
`categorize_tokens()` and pre-computes their character positions in the source string in
a single linear scan. `map_subword_tokens_to_categories()` then uses a monotonically
advancing pointer into those offsets to assign each subword token its parent word's
category in `O(W+T)` time. Special tokens like `[CLS]` and `<s>` are hardcoded to
`"Method Signature"` as the paper treats them as high-importance structural anchors.

### Batched Extraction — `extract_batch_cls()`, `extract_batch_enc_dec()`

Each function tokenizes a full batch with padding, runs one forward pass, and returns
`(tokens, scores)` per sample with padding stripped.

`extract_batch_cls()` handles code search for both models. CodeBERT receives
`(description, code)` pairs so the `[CLS]` token sees both modalities, matching its
fine-tuning setup. CodeT5 receives code only and uses the first token as a CLS proxy
since T5 has no explicit `[CLS]` token.

`extract_batch_enc_dec()` handles summarization using CodeT5 only. The reference
description is passed as decoder input under teacher forcing to match training-time
behaviour, which is what establishes meaningful bi-modal mappings between code tokens
and natural language.

### Aggregation — `build_score_dict()`

Iterates over all extracted results and groups attention scores by `(token, category)`
pair across the entire training set, then computes the mean for each group. This
implements **Equation 3** from the paper — the category-local attention average. The
result is a nested dict `score_dict[token][category] → float`, which gives a separate
importance score for a token depending on the statement context it appears in, rather
than one global average across all contexts.

### Entry Point — `main()`

Wires everything together: loads the task-appropriate training split, loads the
fine-tuned model, runs batched extraction via a `DataLoader` with `num_workers=4` to
overlap data loading with GPU computation, aligns tokens to AST categories per sample,
and writes two output files.

---

## Outputs

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `attention_raw_{model}_{task}.json` | Full per-sample records preserving every token, score, and category assignment. Retained for downstream analysis and debugging. |
| `score_dict_{model}_{task}.json` | Compact `score_dict[token][category] → float` lookup table consumed directly by `simplification.py` at runtime. |

---

## Performance

Inference is batched (`batch_size=32` default, tunable via `--batch-size`) rather than
run one sample at a time, which keeps the GPU saturated. The token-to-category alignment
was rewritten from `O(W×T)` to `O(W+T)` per sample by pre-computing character offsets
once and replacing the original nested `str.find()` loop with a single forward-pass
pointer.

---

author: copilot
body:
`gem push` fails the entire workflow when a version has already been published, causing spurious CI failures on re-runs. The fix captures `gem push` output and silently ignores the "Repushing of gem versions is not allowed" error while still propagating any other failure.

## Changes

- **`.github/actions/build_ruby/entrypoint.sh`**
  - Separate `rake build` and `gem push` into discrete steps (was grouped with a no-op `&& wait`)
  - Capture `gem push` stdout+stderr; on failure, only suppress the known repush error — all other errors still exit with `1`

```shell
bundle exec rake build
GEM_PUSH_OUTPUT=$(gem push pkg/*.gem 2>&1) || {
  echo "$GEM_PUSH_OUTPUT"
  echo "$GEM_PUSH_OUTPUT" | grep -q "Repushing of gem versions is not allowed" || exit 1
}
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ## Problem
> 
> In `.github/actions/build_ruby/entrypoint.sh`, line 36, the `gem push` step fails the entire workflow when a gem version has already been published to RubyGems, with the error:
> 
> ```
> Repushing of gem versions is not allowed.
> Please bump the version number and push a new different release.
> ```
> 
> This causes unnecessary CI failures when a version was already successfully published.
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Update line 36 of `.github/actions/build_ruby/entrypoint.sh` to fail silently when the error is specifically about a gem version already existing, but still fail on any other unexpected errors.
> 
> Replace:
> ```shell
> (bundle exec rake build; gem push pkg/*.gem) && wait
> ```
> 
> With:
> ```shell
> bundle exec rake build
> GEM_PUSH_OUTPUT=$(gem push pkg/*.gem 2>&1) || {
>   echo "$GEM_PUSH_OUTPUT"
>   echo "$GEM_PUSH_OUTPUT" | grep -q "Repushing of gem versions is not allowed" || exit 1
> }
> ```
> 
> **How it works:**
> 1. `gem push` output (stdout + stderr) is captured.
> 2. If `gem push` **succeeds**, execution continues normally.
> 3. If `gem push` **fails**:
>    - The output is printed.
>    - If the error is `"Repushing of gem versions is not allowed"`, the script continues silently (no failure).
>    - If it's any **other** error, the script exits with `exit 1`, preserving normal failure behaviour.
> 
> The no-op `&& wait` (which only applies to backgrounded processes) is also removed as nothing is being backgrounded here.
> 


</details>

### Motivation
- Replace the existing 2D FBM teleporter shader with a richer volumetric-style 3D noise effect to improve the portal visual and animation while keeping the shader a drop-in for the engine.

### Description
- Rewrote `Quake/shaders/teleport_fbm.frag` to replace the old 2D colormap/pattern pipeline with 3D gradient-noise primitives: `hash`, `noised`, and `fbm(vec3)`.
- Implemented a volumetric accumulation pass (ray setup, iterative field warping, SDF/noise mix, and color accumulation) and applied sRGB encoding before outputting `fragColor = vec4(color, alpha)`.
- Preserved engine integration points by continuing to read `v_texcoord` and `u_time` and by producing the same `fragColor` output shape so the shader is a drop-in replacement.
- Tuned iteration counts and constants to produce a stable animated portal effect suited for fragment execution.

---
  Summary

  This PR introduces a composable layer builder system for constructing complex neural network architectures with branching and skip connections, along with
  several new layer primitives.

  BaseLayerGroup / LayerGrouping

  - New BaseLayerGroup class (and LayerGrouping protocol) that wraps an inner Sequential block as a reusable sub-graph layer
  - Provides shared forward pass, gradient application, and weight export logic for group-style layers
  - ResNet refactored to inherit from BaseLayerGroup, eliminating ~50 lines of duplicated gradient slicing code

  RexNet Layer

  - New RexNet layer implementing the ReXNet inverted-residual block (expand → depthwise conv → optional squeeze-and-excite → project)
  - Supports configurable expandRatio, outChannels, strides, and squeeze factor
  - Applies a skip connection when stride == 1 and channels match

  Arithmetic Layers

  - New ArithmeticLayer base class for element-wise tensor operations between two branches of the graph
  - linkId / linkTo system: any layer can expose a linkId and arithmetic layers use findInGraph(to:) to locate the referenced tensor at runtime
  - Concrete implementations: Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide (with inverse support)
  - All layers added to EncodingType for serialization

  Autograd Improvements for Branching Graphs

  - multiplyContext, addContext, divideContext, subtractContext helpers extracted and rewritten to correctly handle branching graphs (where two operands
  share a common ancestor)
  - New branchGradients dictionary on Tensor + setGradientBranch(_:) to accumulate gradients at branch merge points
  - findInGraph(to:) added to Tensor for label-based graph traversal
  - Tensor.input property alias removed; callers now use .graph directly

  Layer Labeling

  - All layers now label their output tensors as <encodingType>-<linkId> in the base forward implementation, enabling graph lookup and debugging

  Tests

  - New ArithmeticTests.swift with unit tests covering forward and backward passes for Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide
  - New LayerTests.swift entries covering RexNet and LayerGroup forward pass shapes

  ---
  Test plan

  - swift test passes (all existing + new tests green)
  - Verify ResNet forward/backward produces same results as before refactor
  - Verify arithmetic layer gradients against manual calculations in ArithmeticTests
  - Test RexNet with and without squeeze-and-excite, and with skip connection enabled/disabled
  - Test model serialization round-trip for Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, RexNet

### Motivation
- Provide a deterministic, bounded recovery search to try to find physically-meaningful parameter combinations that can pass G4 without changing any thresholds, policies, or gate semantics.
- Keep canonical decision logic fail-closed and authoritative while producing reproducible exploratory evidence that can be consumed by operators and governance tooling.
- Surface recovery-search results in the canonical artifacts and report so operators have an explicit, auditable exploratory block without any weakening of guardrails.

### Description
- Added a deterministic recovery search implementation at `scripts/warp-g4-recovery-search.ts` and wired an npm script `warp:full-solve:g4-recovery-search` that enumerates joint lever families (including `warpFieldType`, `gammaGeo`, duty controls, `gammaVanDenBroeck`, `sampler`/`fieldType`/`tau`, and optional `gap_nm`/`shipRadius_m`) using a fixed seed, max-cases, and runtime cap and reuses `updateParameters` + `evaluateQiGuardrail` from the existing pipeline.
- The search writes `artifacts/research/full-solve/g4-recovery-search-2026-02-27.json` and each case row includes inputs, `lhs_Jm3`, `boundComputed_Jm3`, `boundUsed_Jm3`, `marginRatioRaw`, `marginRatioRawComputed`, `applicabilityStatus`, `reasonCode[]`, `rhoSource`, and a deterministic `classificationTag`, plus a top-ranked candidate list and `candidatePassFound` boolean.
- Integrated a fail-closed `recoverySearch` block into `scripts/generate-g4-decision-ledger.ts` that reports artifact path/date, case count, `candidatePassFound`, best candidate summary (if any), and an explicit `failClosedReason` without changing canonical decision classes or gate thresholds.
- Augmented the canonical campaign report generator `scripts/warp-full-solve-campaign.ts` with a `## G4 recovery-search summary` section showing candidate yes/no, best-candidate metrics, and the preserved boundary statement: "This campaign defines falsifiable reduced-order full-solve gates and reproducible evidence requirements; it is not a physical warp feasibility claim." 

### Testing
- Ran canonical regeneration and campaign flows via `npm run warp:full-solve:canonical:bundle` and `npm run warp:full-solve:canonical` which produced the canonical artifacts and left the canonical decision authoritative (counts: PASS=7, FAIL=1, UNKNOWN=0, NOT_READY=0, NOT_APPLICABLE=1; decision=INADMISSIBLE; firstFail=G4). 
- Executed the new recovery search (`npm run warp:full-solve:g4-recovery-search`) which produced `artifacts/research/full-solve/g4-recovery-search-2026-02-27.json` (caseCount=160, `candidatePassFound=false`, best candidate reported), and ran `npm run warp:full-solve:g4-governance-matrix` and `npm run warp:full-solve:g4-decision-ledger` to reconcile artifacts. 
- Ran unit/integration suites with `npx vitest` including the new tests (`tests/warp-g4-recovery-search.spec.ts`) and updated ledger/report tests; targeted and full WARP_AGENTS-required test suites passed (all executed test files passed).

author: claudfuen
body:
## Summary

This PR ships the new **Security → Penetration Tests** capability end-to-end.

It introduces a complete one-time penetration test lifecycle:
- create run
- mocked checkout handoff/return (temporary)
- queue/progress visibility
- run detail page
- markdown/PDF artifact access

## Final architecture

- Frontend calls the existing Comp API client.
- Nest API exposes dedicated penetration-test endpoints.
- Nest API integrates directly with Maced.
- No Next.js API proxy routes are used for this feature.

## User flow

1. User opens **Security → Penetration Tests**.
2. User submits a target URL (and optional repo URL).
3. Frontend calls `POST /v1/security-penetration-tests`.
4. API creates a provider run at Maced and stores org ownership mapping (`organizationId + providerRunId`).
5. User sees the run in list/detail pages with in-progress polling.
6. On completion, user can access markdown and PDF report artifacts.

## Canonical provider contract

- Maced canonical run identifier is **`id`** (no compatibility fallback path in Comp for `runId`).
- Comp stores ownership against `providerRunId` mapped from provider `id`.
- Webhook completion/failure payload handling is aligned to provider `id`.

## What changed

### Frontend (`apps/app`)

- Added Security pages:
  - `/:orgId/security`
  - `/:orgId/security/penetration-tests`
  - `/:orgId/security/penetration-tests/:reportId`
  - `/:orgId/security/penetration-tests/checkout`
- Added polished empty/list/detail states for penetration tests.
- Added SWR hooks and feature-specific client contracts:
  - `usePenetrationTests`
  - `usePenetrationTest`
  - `usePenetrationTestProgress`
  - `useCreatePenetrationTest`
- Added artifact actions on detail page:
  - markdown view
  - PDF download
- Added Security nav/search integration in app shell.
- Added PostHog UI/route gating via `is-security-enabled`.

### Backend (`apps/api`)

- Added dedicated module:
  - `SecurityPenetrationTestsModule`
- Added endpoints:
  - `GET /v1/security-penetration-tests`
  - `POST /v1/security-penetration-tests`
  - `GET /v1/security-penetration-tests/:id`
  - `GET /v1/security-penetration-tests/:id/progress`
  - `GET /v1/security-penetration-tests/:id/report`
  - `GET /v1/security-penetration-tests/:id/pdf`
  - `POST /v1/security-penetration-tests/webhook`
- Added Maced client utility with strict Zod validation for provider request/response contracts.
- Added strict org ownership enforcement on list/get/progress/artifact APIs.
- Added webhook handshake + token verification + idempotency tracking.

### Database (`packages/db`)

- Added ownership mapping model/table:
  - `SecurityPenetrationTestRun`
  - table: `security_penetration_test_runs`
- Ownership mapping key:
  - `organizationId + providerRunId` (unique)

### Docs (`packages/docs`)

- Added customer-facing Penetration Tests docs page.
- Updated OpenAPI docs for penetration-test route and schema names.

## Environment variables

### Required

| Variable | Service | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `MACED_API_KEY` | `apps/api` | API key for Nest API to call Maced provider endpoints. |

### Optional

| Variable | Service | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MACED_API_BASE_URL` | `apps/api` | `https://api.maced.ai` | Override Maced base URL (staging/dev/custom). |
| `SECURITY_PENETRATION_TESTS_WEBHOOK_URL` | `apps/api` | none | Base callback URL used to build webhook target for new runs. |

Notes:
- `is-security-enabled` is a PostHog feature flag (not an env var).
- No feature-specific frontend env vars are required.

## Rollout

- Security tab and Security routes are gated in product UI by PostHog flag:
  - `is-security-enabled`

## Out of scope (intentional)

- Live Stripe checkout + reconciliation (current flow uses mocked checkout).

## Risk/cost note

- Each provider generation has meaningful token cost.
- Generation remains explicit user-driven one-time submit (no automatic recurring runs).

author: dark25
body:
### 🎵 Remove NDK Dependency for Song Recognition

Replaces the entire native C++/FFTW3 Shazam fingerprinting pipeline with a
self-contained pure Kotlin implementation, eliminating the NDK build step and
FFTW3 dependency entirely.

---

### What changed

#### Removed
- `app/src/main/cpp/vibrafp/` — entire native library tree: C++ sources (`vibra.cpp`, `vibra_jni.cpp`, algorithm, audio, utils), CMakeLists, build scripts, headers, and README
- `.github/actions/setup-fftw/action.yml` — custom GitHub Action for building FFTW for all Android ABIs
- FFTW build step removed from `build.yml` (both APK and release jobs) and `build_pr.yml`
- `ndkVersion`, `externalNativeBuild`, NDK `abiFilters`, and CMake release flags removed from `app/build.gradle.kts`
- `System.loadLibrary("vibra_fp")` init block removed from `VibraSignature`

#### Added — `ShazamSignatureGenerator.kt`
Pure Kotlin port of the vibra/Shazam signature algorithm:
- Hanning window computed at class load time via `cos()` (matches the precomputed C++ `HANNIG_MATRIX`)
- Iterative Cooley-Tukey radix-2 DIT FFT (11 stages for 2048-point input), replacing FFTW3
- Ring buffers for FFT outputs and time-spread outputs (256 × 1025 each)
- Frequency spreading (3-point forward max), time spreading (offsets -1, -3, -6)
- Peak recognition with the same 8-neighbor + 14-offset checks as the C++ original
- Signature encoding: per-band peak serialization, 48-byte header, CRC32 via `java.util.zip.CRC32`, Base64 via Android `Base64.NO_WRAP`
- Produces `data:audio/vnd.shazam.sig;base64,...` URI compatible with the Shazam API

#### Updated
- `VibraSignature.kt` — now delegates `fromI16()` to `ShazamSignatureGenerator` instead of JNI; `external` keyword removed
- `MusicRecognitionService.kt` — added `@RequiresApi(Build.VERSION_CODES.CUPCAKE)` annotation to `recordAudio()`

### Impact
- No NDK, no CMake, no FFTW3 build required — CI and local builds are simpler and faster
- APK size reduced (no `.so` native libs bundled)
- All four Android ABI flavors work without per-ABI native library variants

author: wpbonelli
body:
Support writing binary head, budget and grid files.

## Class methods

Add `write()` classmethods to `HeadFile` and `CellBudgetFile`. These write a new file with the given data and return an instance with it open.

### Head files

There are a few syntax variants

```python
# dict keyed by (kstp, kper)
hds = HeadFile.write(
    'output.hds',
    # totim/pertim inferred (dt = 1.0 / time step)
    data={
        (1, 1): h_t1,
        (1, 2): h_t2,
    }
)

# list
hds = HeadFile.write('output.hds', data=[
    {'data': h_t2, 'kstp': 1, 'kper': 1, 'totim': 10.0, 'pertim': 10.0},
    {'data': h_t2, 'kstp': 1, 'kper': 2, 'totim': 20.0, 'pertim': 10.0},
])

# array/list with time as first dimension
# defaults to sequential stress periods: (1,1), (1,2), (1,3), ...
heads = [h_t1, h_t2, h_t3]  # or np.array([h_t1, h_t2, h_t3])
hds = HeadFile.write('output.hds', heads)

# array/list with custom tdis
hds = HeadFile.write('output.hds', heads, kstpkper=[(1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 1)])
```

### Budget files

Again there are variants. The typical case is to use `data` with a list, where each entry has "text", "kper", "kstp", and "data" entries, and "data" is an array, typically grid-shaped. But it can be convenient to use `text` and pass a time-indexed dictionary to `data` to create a file with a single variable.

```python
# just face flows, dict keyed by (kstp, kper)
cbc = CellBudgetFile.write(
    'output.cbc',
    text='FLOW-JA-FACE',
    nlay=3,
    nrow=10,
    ncol=20,
    data={
        (1, 1): q_t1,
        (1, 2): q_t2,
    }
)

# multiple variables, list
cbc = CellBudgetFile.write(
    'output.cbc',
    data=[
        {'data': q_t1, 'kstp': 1, 'kper': 1, 'totim': 10.0,
         'text': 'FLOW-JA-FACE'},
        {'data': ...},
        ...
    ]
)

# array/list with time dimension (grid-shaped data like storage)
# defaults to sequential stress periods: (1,1), (1,2), (1,3), ...
# grid dimensions inferred from array shape
storage = [s_t1, s_t2, s_t3]  # nlay x nrow x ncol arrays
cbc = CellBudgetFile.write('output.cbc', storage, text='STORAGE')

# for face flows, grid dimensions are required since data is 1D
flows = [q_t1, q_t2]  # 1D arrays
cbc = CellBudgetFile.write(
    'output.cbc',
    flows,
    text='FLOW-JA-FACE',
    nlay=3, nrow=10, ncol=20
)
```

If only face flows are provided, the grid shape must be specified with `nlay`/`nrow`/`ncol`, `nlay`/`ncpl`, or `nnodes`. If grid-shaped variables are provided, the grid's shape will be inferred.

## Instance methods

Add instance `export()` methods to

- `MfGrdFile`
- `HeadFile`
- `CellBudgetFile`

These copy the contents of an open file to another, optionally filtering by variable and/or time step, or changing the precision.

### Grid files

```python
from flopy.mf6.utils.binarygrid_util import MfGrdFile

grb = MfGrdFile("model.grb")
grb.export("copy.grb") # copy to another file
grb.export("diff_prec.grb", precision="single") # different precision
```

There is no `write()` method for `MfGrdFile`, as its signature would have been long and complicated to accommodate all grid types.

### Head/budget files

```python
from flopy.utils.binaryfile import HeadFile, CellBudgetFile

# head file
hds = HeadFile("model.hds")
hds.export("copy.hds")  # copy to another file
hds.export("filtered.hds", kstpkper=[(1, 0), (1, 1)])  # filter time steps
hds.export("diff_prec.hds", precision="single")  # different precision

# budget file
cbc = CellBudgetFile("model.cbc")
cbc.export("copy.cbc")
cbc.export("flowja.cbc", text="FLOW-JA-FACE")
cbc.export("bndpkgs.cbc", text=["STORAGE", "CONSTANT HEAD"])
cbc.export("filtered.cbc", kstpkper=[(1, 0)], text="FLOW-JA-FACE")

```

Close #2717

body: Switches the standard of Pa11y we follow from WCAG2AA to WCAG2AAA. In general, I only aim for AA criteria, but for the rules that can be checked automatically, I'd like to strive for AAA as well. Most of the issues reported by Pa11y were color contrast issues on light mode. 1. Mostly because I don't use the site in light mode, so I clearly wasn't paying enough attention. 2. The default Docusaurus theme only strived for WCAG A or AA, not AAA. So we have to override more of the defaults to push it over to the next level. ## Changes | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Links | | | | Sidebar (Light mode) | | | | Preset Badge | | | | Footer | | | In the screenshots above, the differences probably look pretty subtle. However, when actually using the site it's more apparent. ## Chores ### Color Model While doing this, I also migrated most colors from hex to HSL. During development, I always use HSL anyway, I just persisted them as hex out of habit. However, HSL is much more intuitive to work with, and the colors are replaced with hex during the build anyway. ### `!important` When overriding a CSS variable from a theme/plugin, I'm just defaulting to use `!important` now. Historically, I only ever used `!important` when it seemed necessary, but now I find it be simpler when working with third-party variables. ## Related * Pa11y originally added in https://github.com/svg/svgo.dev/pull/54

## Summary

Implements Wave 1 of the Loop-First Evolution plan — the complete Interrogation Engine that takes vague prompts and produces structured specs for execution.

**New module: `aragora/interrogation/`** with 6 components:
- **Decomposer** — breaks vague prompts into concrete dimensions with vagueness scores
- **Researcher** — gathers context from KnowledgeMound and Obsidian per dimension
- **Questioner** — generates prioritized questions with explanations and research context
- **Crystallizer** — converts answers + research into MoSCoW-structured specs

- **Executor** — bridges crystallized specs to HardenedOrchestrator for execution

- `POST /api/v1/interrogation/start` — begin from vague prompt
- `POST /api/v1/interrogation/answer` — answer a question
- `POST /api/v1/interrogation/crystallize` — produce structured spec

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a Windows-first desktop AI assistant scaffold where the LLM is the planner and local Python code is the executor.  
- Use a local Ollama HTTP API as the primary LLM backend with sensible defaults and health-check on startup.  
- Enforce a strict JSON plan/response contract so the LLM only returns structured actions and memory updates.  

### Description
- Added a complete Python application scaffold including `main.py`, `README.md`, and `requirements.txt` and a lightweight `.gitignore`.  
- Implemented an Ollama client (`jarvis_assistant/ollama_client.py`) with defaults `OLLAMA_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:11434` and `OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b-instruct`, startup health-check (`HEAD /` with fallback `GET /api/tags`) and a system prompt that requires JSON output.  
- Added Pydantic models for the LLM plan (`jarvis_assistant/models.py`) describing `intent`, `thought`, `confidence`, `ask_user`, `response`, `memory_update`, and `actions`, plus `ActionResult` for executor feedback.  
- Implemented the orchestration core (`jarvis_assistant/assistant_core.py`), an extensible execution engine (`jarvis_assistant/executor.py`) supporting `cmd`, `powershell`, `launch`, `search`, file I/O, `keyboard`, `mouse`, `window`, `screenshot`, `clipboard`, `browser`, and `wait`, persistent memory store (`jarvis_assistant/memory_store.py`), JSONL logger (`jarvis_assistant/logger.py`), and a Tkinter UI (`jarvis_assistant/ui.py`) with background thread, `Execute/Send`, `STOP` and status indicator.  
- Added persistent memory files under `jarvis_assistant/memory/` (`facts.json` and `preferences.json`) and wiring to apply `memory_update` from LLM.  

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall .` to ensure the codebase compiles and produced no syntax errors (succeeded).  
- Attempted `pip install -r requirements.txt` but installation is blocked in this environment due to network/proxy restrictions (`403 Forbidden`), so runtime dependency import checks could not be completed here.  
- The app performs a startup Ollama health-check at runtime; please run `ollama serve` locally and then start the app with `python main.py` to exercise end-to-end behavior.
